messages:
maria: Quick thread — we need better visibility into routing decisions for tier-based routing + model-variant fallback. Specifically: traces, a small routing header, and one or two console surfaces. Thoughts?

kevin: +1. I think we should emit a compact header at the edge and also create trace spans for the decision path. Example header: `x-rwd-routing: tier=dedicated;region=eu-west;decision=primary:model-7b-v1;fallback=model-4b-quant-v2;reason=capacity`

henry: We must also capture quota semantics. If a request from a Dedicated customer falls back to shared-hosted model, billing and quotas may differ. We need a signal that ties routed requests back to the customer billing record.

ashley: Heads up — writing that header + full trace span for every request will blow up trace storage at high QPS. Can we: sample traces for normal traffic, ALWAYS emit header to logs/metrics, and produce full traces only on fallback or errors? :thinking_face:

kevin: Sampling makes sense. Implementation idea: emit header at the proxy for all requests, stream a small routing metric (`routing_decision{tier,region,policy,served_model}`) to metrics pipeline. Only create detailed trace spans when: fallback==true OR latency delta > 50ms OR error.

sophia: Console UX: add a "Routing" section in the request trace panel that shows a timeline: policy eval -> chosen model -> (optional) fallback. Show the header, policy id, and the model variant name. Allow filter for fallback events. Mock queries we could use for dashboards:```promql
sum(rate(routing_fallbacks_total{policy="tier-routing"}[5m])) by (region, policy)
```And a quick SQL for trace exploration:```sql
SELECT request_id, routing_policy, chosen_model, fallback_reason, latency_ms
FROM request_routing
WHERE ts > now() - interval '1 hour'
ORDER BY ts DESC
LIMIT 50;
```

henry: Security question: should we expose the full model name in customer-visible headers? that could leak internal model naming/versioning. Maybe internal-only by default, opt-in for support.

maria: Good point. Proposal: header `x-rwd-routing` only contains terse tokens (policy id, tier, region, action=fallback/primary). Add an internal-only field `x-rwd-routing-debug` available in traces and to support users who opt-in via account setting.

ashley: If we go opt-in, we need a privacy checklist and rate limits for debug headers. Also make sure KMS/HSM keys unaffected — no PII.

kevin: Implementation plan: 1) edge proxy attaches compact header, 2) routing service emits metrics + sparse traces, 3) trace spans include `route-eval` and `model-start`/`model-serving` with tags for model_variant (internal). I'll draft a header spec and span names.

sophia: For the console: I'll add a small routing timeline widget mock. It should show: policy name, policy id (clickable -> policy config), chosen model (with little badge if fallback), latency delta, and link to raw trace. We'll also add a fallback-rate alert rule.

maria: Billing hook: henry, can you confirm whether fallback requests should count against Dedicated reserved units or fall back to hosted usage rate? We need this before we finalize UI wording.

henry: I'll check with billing/legal and loop back today.

deploy-bot: canary deploy of `routing-propagator:v2` to prod-edge succeeded :white_check_mark:

kevin: Note: routing-propagator v2 already tags decisions as `fallback=true` in metrics. We'll wire that to the dashboard.

ashley: Action on sampling: I'll propose a sampling policy in PR that keeps 1% of normal traces, 100% of fallbacks, and adaptive sampling when error rate > 0.5%.

sophia: UX action: I'll put up a Figma mock and a minimal acceptance criteria doc — will aim for EOD.

maria: Actions summary: kevin -> header + span spec; ashley -> sampling + storage cost estimate; sophia -> console mock + alert rule; henry -> billing semantics. We'll sync tomorrow morning 10am if anyone sees blockers. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
